newsitem.title: USA: Ford explores sale of interests in Budget Rent a Car.
newsitem.headline: Ford explores sale of interests in Budget Rent a Car.

text.p: Ford Motor Co. said Wednesday it may sell its interests in Budget Rent a Car.
"We're looking at the idea that a sale could be done," said Ford spokesman Chris Vinyard.

Ford does not own Budget outright, but has an investment in it consisting of non-voting preferred shares and an option to acquire the car rental agency's common shares, which are owned by investor John Nevin, Vinyard said.
"We could theoretically either sell our option or direct the sale of the common shares through our option," he said.
Ford last year said it would exercise its option and buy the common stock of Budget, then the nation's fourth-largest rental car firm, for an undisclosed sum.
At the same time, Ford took a $437-million after-tax charge against its second-quarter 1996 earnings to write down the value of loans to Budget and Ford's preferred stock in the rental car agency.
Ford's planned purchase of Budget's shares was delayed by a U.S. Federal Trade Commission anti-trust review. "That's where it is now. They're still reviewing it," Vinyard said.
Ford also owns Hertz Corp., the largest U.S. auto rental agency, which is based in Park Ridge, N.J.
Lisle, Ill.-based Budget has been closely allied with Ford for many years and rents mainly Ford vehicles. Ford's planned purchase of the company was meant to improve its performance.

Vinyard declined to comment specifically on an article in Wednesday's Wall Street Journal that said Ford was expected to sell Budget to Team Rental Group Inc., a Daytona Beach, Fla.-based Budget licensee, for about $350 million.
A Team Rental spokesman declined to comment.

Vinyard said Ford is exploring a possible sale of Budget due to rising investor interest in rental car firms. "Interest in the group in the last six to 10 months has increased significantly," Vinyard said.
Three of the top five rental car firms have changed hands in the past four months.
Avis Inc., the second-largest U.S. agency, was acquired last year by HFS Inc. for about $800 million.

Republic Industries Inc., headed by investor Wayne Huizenga, on Monday agreed to buy National Car Rental System Inc. for about $600 million from a private investor group. Republic acquired Alamo Rent a Car late last year.

Vinyard declined to say whether Ford was exploring a possible sale of Hertz, but noted that Hertz has reported record-setting profits for three consecutive years. "We think they'll have another record this year," he said.
Vinyard said the automaker does not plan to make any announcements regarding Budget following Ford's regularly scheduled board meeting Thursday.
Budget Rent a Car officials were not immediately available for comment.
